title: Simulating Agroecology Policy Options for the Resilience of Smallholder Food Security to Climate Shocks
content:
Climate shocks and the agroecology–resilience nexus of smallholders. Summary of key findings: Agroecology increases smallholder resilience capacity by 8.7% in the short term under a decreased rainfall scenario, a projected 11% decline in precipitation reduces resilience by 5.6% and 14.2% in the short and long terms, respectively, and a policy-induced 25% increase in agro-ecological intensity yields a 6.3% increase in resilience under multiple shocks.


ABSTRACT

Climate shocks threaten smallholder resilience capacity in sub-Saharan Africa. This study examines whether agro-ecological practices moderate the climate shock–resilience nexus among smallholders in northern Ghana using a correlated random effects model under five climate scenarios. The results show that current adoption improves resilience and partly offsets rainfall decline, but fails under temperature stress. Under combined shocks, the effects weaken. However, a 25% increase in agro-ecological intensity increases resilience, indicating that scaling adoption is essential for strengthening resilience and building sustainable smallholder food systems.
